Making arrangements·3 min read

Questions before arranging care.

Clarify people, responsibilities, timing and costs before agreeing on support.

In this guide

Understand who will provide support.Put the routine into words.Confirm the practical terms.
Prepare a care note

A clear conversation helps everyone understand the proposed support. These questions are a starting point for discussing arrangements directly with a care provider.

Understand who will provide support.

Ask about the role, relevant qualifications and supervision of the person involved. Match the questions to the actual tasks being discussed.

  • Who will provide care, and what is their role?
  • Which qualifications are relevant to the agreed tasks?
  • Who handles questions, concerns or changes in requirements?

Put the routine into words.

Discuss the timing, tasks and communication in everyday language. Make sure the person receiving support has a say in the routine and understands what has been agreed.

  • What is included during a visit or shift?
  • How are preferences, privacy and personal boundaries respected?
  • How are family updates and handovers managed?

Confirm the practical terms.

Request a clear explanation of costs and the terms that apply to the proposed arrangement. Resolve uncertainty before a service begins.

  • What is included in the quote, and what costs extra?
  • What happens if a visit must change or be cancelled?
  • How will the plan be reviewed if needs change?

Something to take with you.

Keep a record of the agreed scope, contacts and practical terms so everyone has the same understanding.

This guide helps organise a conversation. It does not replace an individual assessment or advice from the treating team.
